questions: Do the three narrow readers of the ledger's hash fields differ from the owner harmfully?
Is consolidating each of them safe?
Does importing ledger_dialect inherit GH #428's over-reading?

findings.finding: gate_provenance.latest_seal_hashes takes two independent whole-file last matches; at 187 of 640 historical states the content and chain hashes came from different entries, and CI HMACs the pair on every push
findings.evidence: replayed the ledger at every historical state; span entry #127-#631

findings.finding: ledger_commitment must NOT be consolidated: its citation pattern accepts Plan|Brief|Artifact (491 entries), so widening the hash pattern admits 45 suffixed session-seal digests as false commitments into a hard ABORT gate
findings.evidence: suffixed form equals the cited file's live hash 0 of 45 times; plain form 99 of 147; stale commitments 74 -> 116

findings.finding: evidence_bundle needs a restructure not a pattern swap: its field dict is consumed by a generic .group(1) loop and CONTENT_HASH_RE has 3 groups, giving the chain field zero gain while appearing fixed
the dialect does not inherit prose-hex capture for the before/after orderings; the BETWEEN ordering does fail, but no corpus entry exhibits it
findings.evidence: 3 constructed orderings; 0 disagreements across 640 entries carrying an inline value
